page: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v5 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the DLDSv5 server family. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The system is provisioned with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes 3686 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results highlight strong multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 93258.02 and a PassMark CPU score of 76019.64. The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptography acceleration, which contribute to a strong PassMark CPU encryption score of 86381.58. Memory performance is robust, showing a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 5005.65 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 134.45 GB/sec. However, single-core performance remains average, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1711.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1899.68.

The D96lds_v5 is qualitatively cost-efficient for highly parallelized, compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, owing to its dense 96-vCPU configuration paired with a modest 192.0 GB of RAM. The server is well-suited for multi-threaded applications such as software compilation, where it achieved a strong Geekbench Clang compilation score of 55338.0, and high-throughput web serving, demonstrated by a static web serving throughput of 64.98 GB/sec. It is also highly capable for database operations and Redis deployments, processing 88.36 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, it is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM text generation, where its average text generation speeds reflect the memory-to-CPU bottleneck.
